how: A starter supplied a proposed symbol and guide that other members answered with construction reports.
Calls recruited members to draw a named mark at specified coordinates.
Members accepted defense work through bare duty reports and reports that helping was working.
The proposed symbol received reports of members drawing its outline and correcting its shape.
Starting and calling are bundled in the same proposal here, so their separation into successive stages is not demonstrated.
The request for help holding off blue received a bare participation report and then a HODL acknowledgment.
Members assessed their strength as tiny or the current fight as unwinnable.
Moving requires an adoptable replacement target because competing scripts and a difficult new location can keep contributors at the old spot.
Members argued over fonts, rotation, colours, size and which Bitcoin image deserved priority.
Members reported outlines, corrected geometry and completion before proposing further expansion.
Guides, coordinates and bitmaps supplied a shared target for pixel work.
A published template supports provisional alignment only when contributors accept the design and adopt the same target.
Members distributed scripts, taught installation, ran alternate accounts and disputed whether automation belonged in the event.
Script users inspected code and assessed trust before running software aimed at holders of valuable assets.
Unattended scripts preserve earlier decisions and require version retirement before a changed plan can become common practice.
A shared target also requires matching offsets and versions across the scripts executing it.
Plans selected in chat return to the public thread and encounter renewed objections, making decision circulation part of coordination.
Staged instructions divide the work into a logo, lettering and background without establishing authority over every placer.
Members repaired changed pixels, committed time and rallied to hold the symbol under pressure.
A declared success became something to protect in the same utterance and in the immediate defense reply.
A preservation script and an update explicitly responding to an invasion connect maintenance pressure to automation.
The record supports defense as a reason for automation without demonstrating that manual capacity was measured and exhausted.
Participants traced suspected attackers and confronted affiliation-based accusations with missing proof, defense accounts and stale scripts.
A changed pixel and an account affiliation leave hostile intention unresolved when the placer reports defense or an outdated target.
Neighbouring groups proposed passage, borders and reciprocal room while other participants disputed the concessions.
Visitors carried treaty requests and discussed a revised design across the room and its chat.
Contributors avoided existing art, moved a drawing, respected borders and stopped an overwriting script.
Threatened overlap prompted explicit requests for contact and for a border rather than only further repainting.
A settled border enables restraint only among placers and tools the agreement reaches or its maker can influence.
A participant answered a demand to stop everyone by explaining that he was only one person helping define the border.
Border agreement was followed by continued-attack complaints and an explicit statement that the helper could not control everyone.
Participants offered relocation help and maintained neighbouring work while others refused help because they recalled invasion.
Relocation and later help were offered as a bargain, but the visible offer does not establish delivered reciprocal help.
Members answered loss with a restart at new coordinates and later updated scripts after being overrun.
A relocation proposal received a report of starting the drawing at new coordinates, supplying a local return from moving to building.
Block-size and SegWit disputes were explicitly recruited into canvas jokes, priorities and accusations of internal struggle.
Existing Bitcoin identity supplied HODL defense language and calls to unite across the BU and CORE split.
April Fools claims and bestowed expert status made authenticity and joking available topics alongside canvas work.
Prank framing can carry substantive disagreement, so the seriousness of individual claims must be assessed within the exchange.
Members asked for a megathread and registered a dedicated canvas subreddit.
The complaint about too many canvas posts explicitly proposed consolidation into a megathread.

statement: Carrying canvas experience into ordinary room exchanges
how: A participant explained hostility in a jobs dispute through lost canvas territory and then apologised to the job seeker.
A logo-based price joke carries canvas experience into ordinary market talk without establishing any effect on price.
Members marked achievement through thanks, their own labour claims and qualified pride in the surviving result.
A completion announcement also celebrated the achievement, allowing both practices to occur in one utterance.
Timelapses, closure announcements and accounts of relocation and lost lettering recorded what survived.
A participant sought a replacement canvas after placement ended, extending earlier discussion of a clone.
Seeking another canvas need not follow documentation because clone discussion began while placement continued.
Members advocated clearing another colour and declared a covert attack on a rival logo.
Participants announced repelling a rival and blamed griefers or Buttcoiners after closure.
